children.text: bahiḥprajño vibhuḥ viśvo hy antaḥprajñas tu taijasaḥ /
children.translated_text: The one whose consciousness is directed outward is <s>Viśva</s>, the all-pervading; while the one whose consciousness is directed inward is <s>Taijasa</s>;

children.text: ghanaprajñaḥ tathā prājña eka eva tridhā smṛtaḥ // MandUpK_1.1 //
children.translated_text: The one who is a mass of consciousness is <s>Prājña</s> — it is one alone, remembered as threefold. (1.1)

children.text: dakṣiṇākṣimukhe viśvo manasy antas tu taijasaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Viśva</s> [resides] in the right eye; <s>Taijasa</s> within the mind;

children.text: ākāśe ca hṛdi prājñas tridhā dehe vyavasthitaḥ // MandUpK_1.2 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> in the space of the heart — thus threefold, established in the body. (1.2)

children.text: viśvaḥ hi sthūlabhuṅ nityaṃ taijasaḥ praviviktabhuk /
children.translated_text: <s>Viśva</s> always enjoys the gross; <s>Taijasa</s> enjoys the subtle;

children.text: ānandabhuk tathā prājñastridhā bhogaṃ nibodhata // MandUpK_1.3 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> likewise enjoys bliss — know the threefold enjoyment. (1.3)

children.text: sthūlaṃ tarpayate viśvaṃ praviviktaṃ tu taijasam /
children.translated_text: The gross satisfies <s>Viśva</s>; the subtle [satisfies] <s>Taijasa</s>;

children.text: ānandaś ca tathā prājñaṃ tridhā tṛptiṃ nibodhata // MandUpK_1.4 //
children.translated_text: And bliss likewise [satisfies] <s>Prājña</s> — know the threefold satisfaction. (1.4)

children.text: triṣu dhāmasu yadbhojyaṃ bhoktā yaś ca prakīrtitaḥ /
children.translated_text: In the three states, that which is enjoyed and who is proclaimed as the enjoyer —

children.text: vadaitadubhayaṃ yas tu sa bhuñjāno na lipyate // MandUpK_1.5 //
children.translated_text: He who knows both of these, he enjoys and is not tainted. (1.5)

children.text: prabhavaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ satām iti viniścayaḥ /
children.translated_text: It is the established conclusion that [the Lord] is the origin of all existing things;

children.text: sarvaṃ janayati prāṇaś ceto 'ṃśūn puruṣaḥ pṛthak // MandUpK_1.6 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇa</s> generates everything; <s>Puruṣa</s> [projects] the rays of consciousness separately. (1.6)

children.text: vibhūtiṃ prasavaṃ tv anye manyante sṛṣṭicintakāḥ /
children.translated_text: Others who reflect on creation think it a manifestation of [divine] glory;

children.text: svapnamāyāsarūpeti sṛṣṭir anyaiḥ vikalpitā // MandUpK_1.7 //
children.translated_text: Yet others imagine creation to be of the nature of dream and illusion. (1.7)

children.text: icchāmātraṃ prabhoḥ sṛṣṭir iti sṛṣṭau viniścitāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who are certain about creation [say] creation is merely the will of the Lord;

children.text: kālāt prasūtiṃ bhūtānāṃ manyante kālacintakāḥ // MandUpK_1.8 //
children.translated_text: Those who contemplate time think the production of beings comes from time. (1.8)

children.text: bhogārthaṃ sṛṣṭir iti anye krīḍārtham iti cāpare /
children.translated_text: Some [say] creation is for enjoyment, and others that it is for sport;

children.text: devasyaiṣa svabhāvo 'yam āptakāmasya kā spṛhā // MandUpK_1.9 //
children.translated_text: This is the very nature of the divine Lord — for one whose desires are fulfilled, what craving [can there be]? (1.9)

children.text: nivṛtteḥ sarvaduḥkhānām īśānaḥ prabhur avyayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The Lord of the cessation of all suffering, the ruler, the imperishable,

children.text: advaitaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ devās turyo vibhuḥ smṛtaḥ // MandUpK_1.10 //
children.translated_text: The non-dual of all beings, the luminous <s>Turya</s> (Fourth), is remembered as all-pervading. (1.10)

children.text: kāryakāraṇabaddhau tāv iṣyete viśvataijasau /
children.translated_text: <s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s> are considered bound by cause and effect;

children.text: prājñaḥ kāraṇabaddhas tu dvau tau turye na sidhyataḥ // MandUpK_1.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> is bound by cause alone — but those two do not exist in <s>Turya</s>. (1.11)

children.text: nātmānaṃ na parāś caiva na satyaṃ na api cānṛtam /
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> cognizes nothing at all — neither self nor others, neither truth nor falsehood;

children.text: prājñaḥ kiñcana saṃvetti turyaṃ tat sarvadṛk sadā // MandUpK_1.12 //
children.translated_text: <s>Turya</s> is always the seer of all. (1.12)

children.text: dvaitasyāgrahaṇaṃ tulyam ubhayoḥ prājñaturyayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The non-apprehension of duality is common to both <s>Prājña</s> and <s>Turya</s>;

children.text: bījanidrāyutaḥ prājñaḥ sā ca turye na vidyate // MandUpK_1.13 //
children.translated_text: <s>Prājña</s> is associated with seed-sleep — but that does not exist in <s>Turya</s>. (1.13)

children.text: svapnanidrāyutāv ādyau prājñas tv asvapnanidrayā /
children.translated_text: The first two [<s>Viśva</s> and <s>Taijasa</s>] are associated with dream and sleep; <s>Prājña</s>, however, has dreamless sleep;

children.text: na nidrāṃ naiva ca svapnaṃ turye paśyanti niścitaḥ // MandUpK_1.14 //
children.translated_text: The resolute [knowers] see neither sleep nor dream in <s>Turya</s>. (1.14)

children.text: anyathā gṛhṇataḥ svapno nidrā tattvam ajānataḥ /
children.translated_text: Dream belongs to one who perceives wrongly; sleep to one who does not know the reality;

children.text: viparyāse tayoḥ kṣīṇe turīyaṃ padam aśnute // MandUpK_1.15 //
children.translated_text: When the error of both is destroyed, the state of <s>Turīya</s> is attained. (1.15)

children.text: anādimāyayā supto yadā jīvaḥ prabudhyate /
children.translated_text: When the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), asleep through beginningless <s>māyā</s>, is awakened,

children.text: ajam anidram asvapnam advaitaṃ budhyate tadā // MandUpK_1.16 //
children.translated_text: Then it realizes the unborn, sleepless, dreamless, non-dual [reality]. (1.16)

children.text: prapañco yadi vidyeta nivarteta na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the phenomenal world existed [as real], it would certainly cease;

children.text: māyāmātram idaṃ dvaitam advaitaṃ paramārthataḥ // MandUpK_1.17 //
children.translated_text: This duality is mere <s>māyā</s> — non-duality alone is the supreme reality. (1.17)

children.text: vikalpo vinivarteta kalpito yadi kenacit /
children.translated_text: The conceptual distinction would cease if it were imagined by anyone;

children.text: upadeśād ayaṃ vādo jñāte dvaitaṃ na vidyate // MandUpK_1.18 //
children.translated_text: This teaching is [merely] for instruction — once [the truth] is known, duality does not exist. (1.18)

children.text: viśvasyātvavivakṣāyām ādisāmānyam utkṛṣṭam /
children.translated_text: When the identity of <s>Viśva</s> [with the letter A] is intended, the excellence lies in being first, [which is] the commonality;

children.text: mātrāsaṃpratipattau syād āptisāmānyam eva ca // MandUpK_1.19 //
children.translated_text: And in the apprehension of the <s>mātrā</s>, the commonality lies in pervasion. (1.19)

children.text: taijasasyotvavijñāna utkarṣo dṛśyate sphuṭam /
children.translated_text: In the identification of <s>Taijasa</s> with [the letter] U, the excellence is clearly seen in elevation;

children.text: mātrāsaṃpratipattau syād ubhayatvaṃ tathā vidham // MandUpK_1.20 //
children.translated_text: And in the apprehension of the <s>mātrā</s>, the commonality lies in partaking of both [qualities]. (1.20)

children.text: makārabhāve prājñasya mānasām anyam utkaṭam /
children.translated_text: In the identification of <s>Prājña</s> with [the letter] M, the excellence lies in measure;

children.text: mātrāsaṃpratipattau tu layasāmānyam eva ca // MandUpK_1.21 //
children.translated_text: And in the apprehension of the <s>mātrā</s>, the commonality lies in dissolution. (1.21)

children.text: triṣu dhāmasu yat tulyaṃ sāmānyaṃ vetti niścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: One who knows with certainty the commonality present in the three states —

children.text: sa pūjyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ vandyaś caiva mahāmuniḥ // MandUpK_1.22 //
children.translated_text: He is worthy of worship by all beings and worthy of homage, that great sage. (1.22)

children.text: akāro nayate viśvam ukāraś cāpi taijasam /
children.translated_text: The letter A leads to <s>Viśva</s>; the letter U also [leads] to <s>Taijasa</s>;

children.text: makāraś ca punaḥ prājñaṃ nāmātre vidyate gatiḥ // MandUpK_1.23 //
children.translated_text: And the letter M again [leads] to <s>Prājña</s> — in the <s>amātra</s> (measureless) there is no going [anywhere]. (1.23)

children.text: oṃkāraṃ pādaśo vidyāt pādā mātrā na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: One should know <s>Oṃkāra</s> quarter by quarter — the quarters are the <s>mātrās</s>, without doubt;

children.text: oṃkāraṃ pādaśo jñātvā na kiñcid api cintayet // MandUpK_1.24 //
children.translated_text: Having known <s>Oṃkāra</s> quarter by quarter, one should not think of anything at all. (1.24)

children.text: yuñjīta praṇave cetaḥ praṇavo brahma nirbhayam /
children.translated_text: One should fix the mind on <s>Praṇava</s>; <s>Praṇava</s> is <s>Brahman</s>, free from fear;

children.text: praṇave nityayuktasya na bhayaṃ vidyate kvacit // MandUpK_1.25 //
children.translated_text: For one ever absorbed in <s>Praṇava</s>, there is no fear anywhere. (1.25)

children.text: praṇavo hy aparaṃ brahma praṇavaś ca paraḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> is indeed the lower <s>Brahman</s>; <s>Praṇava</s> is also remembered as the higher;

children.text: apūrvo 'nantaro 'bāhyo 'naparaḥ praṇavo 'vyayaḥ // MandUpK_1.26 //
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> is without prior [cause], without interior, without exterior, without successor — imperishable. (1.26)

children.text: sarvasya praṇavo hy ādir madhyam antas tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Praṇava</s> is indeed the beginning, middle, and end of all;

children.text: evaṃ hi praṇavaṃ jñātvā vyaśnute tad anantaram // MandUpK_1.27 //
children.translated_text: Having known <s>Praṇava</s> thus, one attains that [<s>Brahman</s>] immediately. (1.27)

children.text: praṇavaṃ hīśvaraṃ vidyāt sarvasya hṛdi saṃsthitam /
children.translated_text: One should know <s>Praṇava</s> as the Lord established in the heart of all;

children.text: sarvavyāpinam oṃkāraṃ matvā dhīro na śocati // MandUpK_1.28 //
children.translated_text: Knowing <s>Oṃkāra</s> as all-pervading, the wise one does not grieve. (1.28)

children.text: amātro 'nantamātraś ca dvaitasyopaśamaḥ śivaḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is without <s>mātrā</s>, of infinite <s>mātrās</s>, the cessation of duality, auspicious —

children.text: oṃkāro vidito yena sa munir netāro janaḥ // MandUpK_1.29 //
children.translated_text: One by whom <s>Oṃkāra</s> is thus known is a sage, not any other person. (1.29)

children.text: vaitathyaṃ sarvabhāvānāṃ svapna āhur manīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise declare the unreality of all things in dream,

children.text: antaḥsthānāt tu bhāvānāṃ saṃvṛtatvena hetunā // MandUpK_2.1 //
children.translated_text: Because of the internal location of those things, and because of the reason that they are enclosed. (2.1)

children.text: adīrghatvāc ca kālasya gatvā deśān na paśyati /
children.translated_text: And because of the shortness of time, upon going one does not see those places;

children.text: pratibuddhaś ca vai sarvas tasmin deśe na vidyate // MandUpK_2.2 //
children.translated_text: And indeed everyone, upon waking, is not found in that place. (2.2)

children.text: abhāvaś ca rathādīnāṃ śrūyate nyāyapūrvakam /
children.translated_text: The non-existence of chariots and the like is heard of with logical reasoning;

children.text: vaitathyaṃ tena vai prāptaṃ svapna āhuḥ prakāśitam // MandUpK_2.3 //
children.translated_text: Thereby unreality is attained — they say it is revealed in dream. (2.3)

children.text: antasthānāt tu bhedānāṃ tasmāj jāgarite smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Because of the internal nature of the differences, therefore in the waking state too it is remembered;

children.text: yathā tatra tathā svapne saṃvṛtatvena bhidyate // MandUpK_2.4 //
children.translated_text: As it is there [in dream], so in waking — [things] are differentiated by being enclosed. (2.4)

children.text: svapnajāgaritasthāne hy ekam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise declare the states of dream and waking to be one and the same,

children.text: bhedānāṃ hi samatvena prasiddhenaiva hetunā // MandUpK_2.5 //
children.translated_text: Because of the well-established reason of the sameness of differences. (2.5)

children.text: ādāvante ca yan nāsti vartamāne 'pi tat tathā /
children.translated_text: That which does not exist at the beginning and end does not [truly] exist in the present either;

children.text: vitathaiḥ sadṛśāḥ santo 'vitathā iva lakṣitāḥ // MandUpK_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Though resembling unreal things, they are perceived as if they were real. (2.6)

children.text: saprayojanatā teṣāṃ svapne vipratipadyate /
children.translated_text: Their purposefulness is contradicted in dream;

children.text: tasmād ādyantavatvena mithyaiva khalu te smṛtāḥ // MandUpK_2.7 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of having a beginning and end, they are indeed remembered as false. (2.7)

children.text: apūrvaṃ sthānidharmo hi yathā svarganivāsinām /
children.translated_text: The unfamiliar nature [of things] is the characteristic of the dwellers of heaven;

children.text: tānayaṃ prekṣate gatvā yathaiveha suśikṣitaḥ // MandUpK_2.8 //
children.translated_text: One goes and perceives them, just as one well-trained [perceives things] here [in waking]. (2.8)

children.text: svapnavṛttāv api tv antaś cetasā kalpitaṃ tv asat /
children.translated_text: Even in the dream state, what is imagined internally by the mind is unreal,

children.text: bahiś cetogṛhītaṃ sad dṛṣṭaṃ vaitathyam etayoḥ // MandUpK_2.9 //
children.translated_text: While what is grasped externally by the mind is [taken as] real — [but] unreality is seen in both. (2.9)

children.text: jāgradvṛttāvapi tv antaś cetasā kalpitaṃ tv asat /
children.translated_text: Even in the waking state, what is imagined internally by the mind is unreal,

children.text: bahiścetogṛhītaṃ sad yuktaṃ vaitathyam etayoḥ // MandUpK_2.10 //
children.translated_text: While what is grasped externally by the mind is [taken as] real — [yet] it is reasonable that both are unreal. (2.10)

children.text: ubhayor api vaitathyaṃ bhedānāṃ sthānayor yadi /
children.translated_text: If the unreality of things in both states [is established],

children.text: ka etān budhyate bhedān ko vai teṣāṃ vikalpakaḥ // MandUpK_2.11 //
children.translated_text: Who cognizes these things? Who indeed is their imaginer? (2.11)

children.text: kalpayaty ātmanātmānam ātmā devaḥ svamāyayā /
children.translated_text: The <s>Ātman</s>, the luminous Lord, imagines himself by himself through his own <s>māyā</s>;

children.text: sa eva budhyate bhedān iti vedāntaniścayaḥ // MandUpK_2.12 //
children.translated_text: He alone cognizes the differences — this is the conclusion of <s>Vedānta</s>. (2.12)

children.text: vikaroty aparān bhāvān antaścitte vyavasthitān /
children.translated_text: The Lord projects other things established within the mind,

children.text: niyatāṃś ca bahiścitta evaṃ kalpayate prabhuḥ // MandUpK_2.13 //
children.translated_text: And those that are determined externally from the mind — thus he imagines. (2.13)

children.text: cittakālā hi ye 'ntas tu dvayakālāś ca ye bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that exist internally for the duration of thought, and those that exist externally for the duration of two [moments] —

children.text: kalpitā eva te sarve viśeṣo nānyahetukaḥ // MandUpK_2.14 //
children.translated_text: All of them are merely imagined; there is no distinction due to any other cause. (2.14)

children.text: avyaktā eva ye 'ntas tu sphuṭā eva ca ye bahiḥ /
children.translated_text: Those that are unmanifest internally and those that are clearly manifest externally —

children.text: kalpitā eva te sarve viśeṣas tv indriyāntare // MandUpK_2.15 //
children.translated_text: All of them are merely imagined; the distinction is only due to the difference of sense organs. (2.15)

children.text: jīvaṃ kalpayate pūrvaṃ vaco bhāvān pṛthagvidhān /
children.translated_text: First [the Lord] imagines the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul), then various objects,

children.text: bāhyān ādhyātmikāṃś caiva yathāvidyas tathāsmṛtiḥ // MandUpK_2.16 //
children.translated_text: External and internal; as is one's knowledge, so is one's memory. (2.16)

children.text: aniścitā yathā rajjur andhakāre vikalpitā /
children.translated_text: Just as a rope, undetermined in darkness, is imagined

children.text: sarpadhārādibhir bhāvais tadvad ātmā vikalpitaḥ // MandUpK_2.17 //
children.translated_text: As a snake, a stream of water, and other things — so the <s>Ātman</s> is imagined. (2.17)

children.text: niścitāyāṃ yathā rajjvāṃ vikalpo vinivartate /
children.translated_text: Just as, when the rope is determined, the imagination ceases

children.text: rajjur eveti cādvaitaṃ tadvad ātmaviniścayaḥ // MandUpK_2.18 //
children.translated_text: And there arises the non-dual [knowledge] that 'it is a rope only' — so is the ascertainment of the <s>Ātman</s>. (2.18)

children.text: prāṇādibhir anantaiś ca bhāvair etair vikalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: [The <s>Ātman</s>] is imagined as <s>prāṇa</s> and other infinite entities;

children.text: māyaiṣā tasya devasya yayā saṃmohitaḥ svayam // MandUpK_2.19 //
children.translated_text: This is the <s>māyā</s> of that luminous Lord, by which he himself is deluded. (2.19)

children.text: prāṇa iti prāṇavido bhūtānīti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know <s>prāṇa</s> [call it] '<s>prāṇa</s>'; those who know the elements [call them] 'elements';

children.text: guṇā iti guṇavidas tattvānīti ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.20 //
children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>guṇas</s> [call them] '<s>guṇas</s>'; those who know the <s>tattvas</s> [call them] '<s>tattvas</s>.' (2.20)

children.text: pādā iti pādavido viṣayā iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know the quarters [call them] 'quarters'; those who know objects [call them] 'objects';

children.text: lokā iti lokavido devā iti ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.21 //
children.translated_text: Those who know the worlds [call them] 'worlds'; those who know the gods [call them] 'gods.' (2.21)

children.text: vedā iti vedavido yajñā iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know the <s>Vedas</s> [call it] 'the <s>Vedas</s>'; those who know sacrifices [call them] 'sacrifices';

children.text: bhokteti ca bhoktṛvido bhojyam iti ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2. 22 //
children.translated_text: Those who know the enjoyer [call it] 'the enjoyer'; those who know the enjoyed [call it] 'the enjoyed.' (2.22)

children.text: sūkṣma iti sūkṣmavidaḥ sthūla iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know the subtle [call it] 'subtle'; those who know the gross [call it] 'gross';

children.text: mūrta iti mūrtavido 'mūrta iti ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.23 //
children.translated_text: Those who know form [call it] 'form'; those who know the formless [call it] 'formless.' (2.23)

children.text: kāla iti kālavido diśa iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know time [call it] 'time'; those who know directions [call them] 'directions';

children.text: vādā iti vādavido bhuvanānīti tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.24 //
children.translated_text: Those who know doctrines [call them] 'doctrines'; those who know the worlds [call them] 'worlds.' (2.24)

children.text: mana iti manovido buddhir iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know mind [call it] 'mind'; those who know intellect [call it] 'intellect';

children.text: cittam iti cittavido dharmādharmau ca tadvidaḥ // MandUpK_2.25 //
children.translated_text: Those who know consciousness [call it] 'consciousness'; those who know <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s> [call them] the same. (2.25)

children.text: pañcaviṃśaka ity eke ṣaḍviśa iti cāpare /
children.translated_text: Some say twenty-five [principles], others say twenty-six;

children.text: ekatriṃśaka ity āhur ananta iti cāpare // MandUpK_2.26 //
children.translated_text: some declare thirty-one, while others [say they are] infinite. ||2.26||

children.text: lokāṃl lokavidaḥ prāhur āśramā iti tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know the worlds speak of worlds; those who know the stages of life, of <s>āśramas</s>;

children.text: strīpuṃnapuṃsakaṃ laiṅgāḥ parāparam athāpare // MandUpK_2.27 //
children.translated_text: those who know genders [speak of] female, male, and neuter; those who know the higher and lower, of the supreme and inferior. ||2.27||

children.text: sṛṣṭir iti sṛṣṭivido laya iti ca tadvidaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who know creation speak of creation; those who know dissolution, of dissolution;

children.text: sthitir iti sthitividaḥ sarve ceha tu sarvadā // MandUpK_2.28 //
children.translated_text: those who know permanence, of permanence — but all these exist here always. ||2.28||

children.text: yaṃ bhāvaṃ darśayed yasya taṃ bhāvaṃ sa tu paśyati /
children.translated_text: Whatever state [of reality] one demonstrates to someone, that state he perceives;

children.text: taṃ cāvati sa bhūtvāsau tadgrahaḥ samupaiti tam // MandUpK_2.29 //
children.translated_text: and that [state], having become his protector, approaches him as his conviction. ||2.29||

children.text: etair eṣo 'pṛthagbhāvaiḥ pṛthag eveti lakṣitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This [Self], though non-different from these [states], is characterized as if distinct;

children.text: evaṃ yo veda tattvena kalpayet so 'viśaṅkitaḥ // MandUpK_2.30 //
children.translated_text: one who knows the truth thus may imagine without hesitation. ||2.30||

children.text: svapnamāye yathā dṛṣṭaṃ gandharvanagaraṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as things seen in dream and illusion, just as a <s>gandharva</s> city (mirage) —

children.text: tathā viśvam idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ vedānteṣu vicakṣaṇaiḥ // MandUpK_2.31 //
children.translated_text: so has this entire universe been seen by the wise in the <s>Vedānta</s>. ||2.31||

children.text: na nirodho na cotpattir na baddho na ca sādhakaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no cessation, no origination; no one in bondage, no one practicing;

children.text: na mumukṣur na vai mukta ity eṣā paramārthatā // MandUpK_2.32 //
children.translated_text: no one seeking liberation, no one liberated — this is the ultimate truth. ||2.32||

children.text: bhāvair asadbhir evāyam advayena ca kalpitaḥ /
children.translated_text: This [Self] is imagined through non-existent entities and through the non-dual;

children.text: bhāvā apy advayenaiva tasmād advayatā śivā // MandUpK_2.33 //
children.translated_text: the entities too [are imagined] through the non-dual alone — therefore non-duality is auspicious. ||2.33||

children.text: nātmabhāvena nānedaṃ na svenāpi kathañcana /
children.translated_text: This [world] is neither by the nature of the Self nor by its own nature in any way;

children.text: na pṛthaṅ nāpṛthak kiñcid iti tattvavido viduḥ // MandUpK_2.34 //
children.translated_text: nothing is either separate or non-separate — thus know the knowers of truth. ||2.34||

children.text: vītarāgabhayakrodhair munibhir vedapāragaiḥ /
children.translated_text: By sages free from passion, fear, and anger, who have crossed to the far shore of the <s>Vedas</s>,

children.text: nirvikalpo hy ayaṃ dṛṣṭaḥ prapañcopaśamo 'dvayaḥ // MandUpK_2.35 //
children.translated_text: this has been seen: free from conceptual construction, the cessation of the phenomenal world, non-dual. ||2.35||

children.text: tasmād evaṃ viditvainam advaite yojayet smṛtim /
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowing thus, one should fix one's awareness on non-duality;

children.text: advaitaṃ samanuprāpya jaḍavallokam ācaret // MandUpK_2.36 //
children.translated_text: having attained non-duality, one should move in the world as if inert. ||2.36||

children.text: niḥstutir nirnamaskāro niḥsvadhākāra eva ca /
children.translated_text: Without praise, without salutation, and without the <s>svadhā</s> call,

children.text: calācalaniketaś ca yatir yādṛcchiko bhavet // MandUpK_2.37 //
children.translated_text: the renunciant, whose abode is both moving and unmoving, should live spontaneously. ||2.37||

children.text: tattvam ādhyātmikaṃ dṛṣṭvā tattvaṃ dṛṣṭvā tu bāhyataḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen the truth internally and having seen the truth externally,

children.text: tattvībhūtas tadārāmas tattvād apracyuto bhavet // MandUpK_2.38 //
children.translated_text: having become truth itself, delighting in truth, one should not fall away from truth. ||2.38||

children.text: upāsanāśrito dharmo jāte brahmaṇi vartate /
children.translated_text: The <s>dharma</s> dependent on worship pertains to the born <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: prāgutpatter ajaṃ sarvaṃ tenāsau kṛpaṇaḥ smṛtaḥ // MandUpK_3.1 //
children.translated_text: before origination, all is unborn — therefore that one is called pitiable. ||3.1||

children.text: ato vakṣyāmy akārpaṇyam ajāti samatāṃ gatam /
children.translated_text: Hence I shall declare that which is free from pity — the unborn that has attained sameness —

children.text: yathā na jāyate kiñcij jāyamānaṃ samantataḥ // MandUpK_3.2 //
children.translated_text: how nothing whatsoever is born, though appearing to be born on every side. ||3.2||

children.text: ātmā hy ākāśavajjīvair ghaṭākāśair ivoditaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>Ātman</s> is like space; the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls) are said to be like the space within pots;

children.text: ghaṭādivac ca saṃghātair jātāv etan nidarśanam // MandUpK_3.3 //
children.translated_text: the aggregates are like the pots — this is the illustration regarding birth. ||3.3||

children.text: ghaṭādiṣu pralīneṣu ghaṭākāśādayo yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as when pots and the like are destroyed, the space within the pots

children.text: ākāśe saṃpralīyante tadvaj jīvā ihātmani // MandUpK_3.4 //
children.translated_text: merges into [universal] space, so here the <s>jīvas</s> merge into the <s>Ātman</s>. ||3.4||

children.text: yathaikasmin ghāṭākāśe rajodhūmādibhir yute /
children.translated_text: Just as when the space in one pot is pervaded by dust, smoke, and the like,

children.text: na sarve saṃprayujyante tadvaj jīvāḥ sukhādibhiḥ // MandUpK_3.5 //
children.translated_text: not all [pot-spaces] are pervaded — so too the <s>jīvas</s> with pleasure and the like. ||3.5||

children.text: rūpakāryasamākhyāś ca bhidyante tatra tatra vai /
children.translated_text: Forms, functions, and names differ here and there;

children.text: ākāśasya na bhedo 'sti tadvaj jīveṣu nirṇayaḥ // MandUpK_3.6 //
children.translated_text: but there is no differentiation of space — such is the determination regarding the <s>jīvas</s>. ||3.6||

children.text: nākāśasya ghaṭākāśo vikārāvayavau yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as pot-space is neither a modification nor a part of [universal] space,

children.text: naivātmanaḥ sadā jīvo vikārāvayavau tathā // MandUpK_3.7 //
children.translated_text: so the <s>jīva</s> is never a modification or a part of the <s>Ātman</s>. ||3.7||

children.text: yathā bhavati bālānāṃ gaganaṃ malinaṃ malaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as the sky appears soiled with impurities to children,

children.text: tathā bhavaty abuddhānām ātmāpi malino malaiḥ // MandUpK_3.8 //
children.translated_text: so the <s>Ātman</s> appears impure with impurities to the unwise. ||3.8||

children.text: maraṇe saṃbhave caiva gatyāgamanayor api /
children.translated_text: In death and in birth, in going and in coming,

children.text: sthitau sarvaśarīreṣu ākāśenāvilakṣaṇaḥ // MandUpK_3.9 //
children.translated_text: and in existing in all bodies — [the <s>Ātman</s>] is not different from space. ||3.9||

children.text: saṃghātāḥ svapnavat sarve ātmamāyāvisarjitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All aggregates are like dreams, projected by the <s>māyā</s> of the <s>Ātman</s>;

children.text: ādhikye sarvasāmye vā nopapattir hi vidyate // MandUpK_3.10 //
children.translated_text: whether one be superior or all be equal, there is no logical proof [of their reality]. ||3.10||

children.text: rasādayo hi ye kośā vyākhyātās taittirīyake /
children.translated_text: The sheaths — of food and the rest — that are described in the <s>Taittirīyaka</s> [Upaniṣad],

children.text: teṣām ātmā paro jīvaḥ khaṃ yathā saṃprakāśitaḥ // MandUpK_3.11 //
children.translated_text: of these, the supreme Self, the <s>jīva</s>, is revealed to be like space. ||3.11||

children.text: dvayor dvayor madhujñāne paraṃ brahma prakāśitam /
children.translated_text: In the knowledge of the two honeys, the supreme <s>Brahman</s> is revealed,

children.text: pṛthivyāmudare caiva yathākāśaḥ prakāśitaḥ // MandUpK_3.12 //
children.translated_text: just as space is revealed within the earth and within the body. ||3.12||

children.text: jīvātmanor ananyatvam abhedena praśasyate /
children.translated_text: The non-difference of the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>Ātman</s> is praised in terms of identity;

children.text: nānātvaṃ nindyate yac ca tad evaṃ hi samañjasam // MandUpK_3.13 //
children.translated_text: plurality is condemned — and this alone is consistent. ||3.13||

children.text: jīvātmanoḥ pṛthaktvaṃ yat prāgutpatteḥ prakīrtitam /
children.translated_text: The separateness of the <s>jīva</s> and the <s>Ātman</s> that is declared before origination

children.text: bhaviṣyadvṛtyā gauṇaṃ tan mukhyatvaṃ hi na yujyate // MandUpK_3.14 //
children.translated_text: is figurative, using a future tense — it cannot be primary. ||3.14||

children.text: mṛllohavisphuliṅgādyaiḥ sṛṣṭir yā coditānyathā /
children.translated_text: The creation taught differently through [the illustrations of] clay, iron, sparks, and the like —

children.text: upāyaḥ so 'vatārāya nāsti bhedaḥ kathañcana // MandUpK_3.15 //
children.translated_text: that is a means of introduction; there is no difference whatsoever. ||3.15||

children.text: āśramāstrividhā hīnamadhyamotkṛṣṭadṛṣṭayaḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>āśramas</s> are of three kinds — for those of inferior, middling, and superior vision;

children.text: upāsanopadiṣṭeyaṃ tadartham anukampayā // MandUpK_3.16 //
children.translated_text: this worship is taught for their sake, out of compassion. ||3.16||

children.text: svasiddhāntavyavasthāsu dvaitino niścitā dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: The dualists, firmly established in the tenets of their own systems,

children.text: parasparaṃ virudhyante tairayaṃ na virudhyate // MandUpK_3.17 //
children.translated_text: contradict one another; this [<s>Advaita</s> teaching] is not contradicted by them. ||3.17||

children.text: advaitaṃ paramārtho hi dvaitaṃ tadbheda ucyate /
children.translated_text: Non-duality is the ultimate reality; duality is said to be its modification.

children.text: teṣām ubhayathā dvaitaṃ tenāyaṃ na viruddhyate // MandUpK_3.18 //
children.translated_text: For them there is duality in either case — therefore this [<s>Advaita</s>] is not contradicted. ||3.18||

children.text: māyayā bhidyate hy etan nānyathājaṃ kathañcana /
children.translated_text: For this [world] is divided by <s>māyā</s>, not otherwise — since it is unborn in any way;

children.text: tattvato bhidyamāne hi martyatām amṛtaṃ vrajet // MandUpK_3.19 //
children.translated_text: if it were divided in reality, the immortal would become mortal. ||3.19||

children.text: ajātasyaiva bhāvasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The disputants wish to establish the birth of an entity that is unborn;

children.text: ajāto hy amṛto bhāvo martyatāṃ katham eṣyati // MandUpK_3.20 //
children.translated_text: how shall an entity that is unborn and immortal come to mortality? ||3.20||

children.text: na bhavaty amṛtaṃ martyaṃ na martyam amṛtaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The immortal does not become mortal, nor does the mortal become immortal;

children.text: prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathañcid bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_3.21 //
children.translated_text: a change of one's fundamental nature will never come about in any way. ||3.21||

children.text: svabhāvenāmṛto yasya bhāvo gacchati martyatām /
children.translated_text: For one whose entity is by nature immortal — if it were to undergo mortality,

children.text: kṛtakenāmṛtas tasya kathaṃ sthāsyati niścalaḥ // MandUpK_3.22 //
children.translated_text: how would the immortal, being artificially produced, remain unchanging? ||3.22||

children.text: bhūtato 'bhūtato vāpi sṛjyamāne samā śrutiḥ /
children.translated_text: Whether [things are] created from the existent or from the non-existent, the scripture is equally applicable;

children.text: niścitaṃ yuktiyuktaṃ ca yat tad bhavati netarat // MandUpK_3.23 //
children.translated_text: what is ascertained and supported by reasoning is true, and nothing else. ||3.23||

children.text: neha nāneti cāmnāyād indro māyābhir ity api /
children.translated_text: 'There is no plurality here' — so says the scripture; and '<s>Indra</s> [appears manifold] through <s>māyā</s>s';

children.text: ajāyamāno bahudhā māyayā jāyate tu saḥ // MandUpK_3.24 //
children.translated_text: 'Though unborn, He is born in manifold ways through <s>māyā</s>.' ||3.24||

children.text: saṃbhūter apavādāc ca saṃbhavaḥ pratiṣidhyate /
children.translated_text: By the denial of origination, origination is negated;

children.text: ko nv enaṃ janayed iti kāraṇaṃ pratiṣidhyate // MandUpK_3.25 //
children.translated_text: 'Who indeed could produce Him?' — thereby the cause is negated. ||3.25||

children.text: sa eṣa neti netīti vyākhyātaṃ nihnute yataḥ /
children.translated_text: It is explained as 'He is not this, not this' — since it negates everything;

children.text: sarvam agrāhyabhāvena hetunājaṃ prakāśate // MandUpK_3.26 //
children.translated_text: by the reasoning that everything is of ungraspable nature, the unborn shines forth. ||3.26||

children.text: sato hi māyayā janma yujyate na tu tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: For the existent, birth through <s>māyā</s> is tenable, but not in reality;

children.text: tattvato jāyate yasya jātaṃ tasya hi jāyate // MandUpK_3.27 //
children.translated_text: for one whose birth occurs in reality, the born is indeed already born. ||3.27||

children.text: asato māyayā janma tattvato naiva yujyate /
children.translated_text: For the non-existent, birth through <s>māyā</s> is not at all tenable;

children.text: vandhyāputro na tattvena māyayā vāpi jāyate // MandUpK_3.28 //
children.translated_text: a barren woman's son is born neither in reality nor through <s>māyā</s>. ||3.28||

children.text: yathā svapne dvayābhāsaṃ spandate māyayā manaḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in a dream the mind vibrates through <s>māyā</s> with the appearance of duality,

children.text: tathā jāgraddvayābhāsaṃ spandate māyayā manaḥ // MandUpK_3.29 //
children.translated_text: so in the waking state the mind vibrates through <s>māyā</s> with the appearance of duality. ||3.29||

children.text: advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ manaḥ svapne na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no doubt that the mind in dream is non-dual, though appearing as dual;

children.text: advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ tathā jāgran na saṃśayaḥ // MandUpK_3.30 //
children.translated_text: there is no doubt that the mind in waking too is non-dual, though appearing as dual. ||3.30||

children.text: manodṛśyam idaṃ dvaitaṃ yat kiñcit sacarācaram /
children.translated_text: All this duality — whatever moves and is motionless — is perceived by the mind;

children.text: manaso hy amanībhāve dvaitaṃ naivopalabhyate // MandUpK_3.31 //
children.translated_text: for when the mind becomes no-mind, duality is never perceived. ||3.31||

children.text: ātmasatyānubodhena na saṃkalpayate yadā /
children.translated_text: When, by the realization of the truth of the <s>Ātman</s>, one no longer imagines,

children.text: amanastāṃ tadā yāti grāhyābhāve tadagraham // MandUpK_3.32 //
children.translated_text: the mind attains the state of no-mind; in the absence of things to be grasped, it becomes non-grasping. ||3.32||

children.text: akalpamajaṃ jñānaṃ jñeyābhinnaṃ pracakṣate /
children.translated_text: Knowledge that is free from imagination, unborn, and non-different from the knowable — they declare;

children.text: brahma jñeyam ajaṃ nityam ajenājaṃ vibudhyate // MandUpK_3.33 //
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s> is the knowable, unborn, eternal — the unborn is known by the unborn. ||3.33||

children.text: nigṛhītasya manaso nirvikalpasya dhīmataḥ /
children.translated_text: The activity of the restrained mind of the wise one, free from conceptual construction,

children.text: pracāraḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ suṣupte 'nyo na tatsamaḥ // MandUpK_3.34 //
children.translated_text: is to be understood [as distinct]; it is other than [the state in] deep sleep — nothing is the same as that. ||3.34||

children.text: līyate hi suṣupte tan nigṛhītaṃ na līyate /
children.translated_text: For [the mind] dissolves in deep sleep; the restrained [mind] does not dissolve;

children.text: tad eva nirbhayaṃ brahma jñānalokaṃ samantataḥ // MandUpK_3.35 //
children.translated_text: that itself is the fearless <s>Brahman</s>, the light of knowledge on all sides. ||3.35||

children.text: ajam anindram asvapnam anāmakam arūpakam /
children.translated_text: Unborn, free from sleep, free from dream, without name, without form,

children.text: sakṛdvibhātaṃ sarvajñaṃ nopacāraḥ kathañcana // MandUpK_3.36 //
children.translated_text: once and for all resplendent, omniscient — there is no practice of any kind whatsoever [needed]. ||3.36||

children.text: sarvābhilāpavigataḥ sarvacintāsamutthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Beyond all expression, risen above all thought,

children.text: supraśāntaḥ sakṛjjyotiḥ samādhir acalo 'bhayaḥ // MandUpK_3.37 //
children.translated_text: perfectly tranquil, eternally luminous — such is <s>samādhi</s>: unshakable and fearless. ||3.37||

children.text: graho na tatra notsargaś cintā yatra na vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is no grasping or letting go where thought does not exist;

children.text: ātmasaṃsthaṃ tadā jñānam ajāti samatāṃ gatam // MandUpK_3.38 //
children.translated_text: then knowledge, established in the Self, is unborn and has attained sameness. ||3.38||

children.text: asparśayogo vai nāma durdarśaḥ sarvayogibhiḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Asparśa-yoga</s> (the yoga of non-contact) by name is difficult to perceive for all <s>yogins</s>;

children.text: yogino bibhyati hy asmād abhaye bhayadarśinaḥ // MandUpK_3.39 //
children.translated_text: the <s>yogins</s> indeed fear it, seeing danger where there is none. ||3.39||

children.text: manaso nigrahāyattam abhayaṃ sarvayoginām /
children.translated_text: For all <s>yogins</s>, fearlessness depends on the restraint of the mind,

children.text: duḥkhakṣayaḥ prabodhaś cāpy akṣayā śāntir eva ca // MandUpK_3.40 //
children.translated_text: the destruction of suffering, awakening, and imperishable peace. ||3.40||

children.text: utseka udadher yadvat kuśāgreṇaikabindunā /
children.translated_text: Just as draining the ocean drop by drop with the tip of a <s>kuśa</s> grass blade —

children.text: manaso nigrahas tadvad bhaved aparikhedataḥ // MandUpK_3.41 //
children.translated_text: so would the restraint of the mind be, [achieved] without weariness. ||3.41||

children.text: upāyena nigṛhṇīyād vikṣiptaṃ kāmabhogayoḥ /
children.translated_text: The [mind] that is distracted by desires and pleasures should be restrained by proper means;

children.text: suprasannaṃ laye caiva yathā kāmo layas tathā // MandUpK_3.42 //
children.translated_text: and [the mind] that is well-tranquil in absorption [should also be watched] — for <s>laya</s> (absorption) is as [problematic] as desire. ||3.42||

children.text: duḥkhaṃ sarvam anusmṛtya kāmabhogān nivartayet /
children.translated_text: Remembering that all is suffering, one should turn away from sense pleasures;

children.text: ajaṃ sarvamanusmṛtya jātaṃ naiva tu paśyati // MandUpK_3.43 //
children.translated_text: Remembering that all is unborn, one does not see anything as born. // <s>MandUpK</s> 3.43 //

children.text: laye saṃbodhayec cittaṃ vikṣiptaṃ śamayet punaḥ /
children.translated_text: When [the mind] lapses into torpor, one should rouse it; when distracted, one should again pacify it;

children.text: sakaṣāyaṃ vijānīyāt samaprāptaṃ na cālayet // MandUpK_3.44 //
children.translated_text: One should know when it has defilements; when it has reached equanimity, one should not disturb it. // <s>MandUpK</s> 3.44 //

children.text: nāsvādayet sukhaṃ tatra niḥsaṅgaḥ prajñayā bhavet /
children.translated_text: One should not savor pleasure therein; through wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), one should become detached;

children.text: niścalaṃ niścarac cittam ekīkuryāt prayatnataḥ // MandUpK_3.45 //
children.translated_text: The mind that is steady yet wandering outward should be unified with effort. // <s>MandUpK</s> 3.45 //

children.text: yadā na līyate cittaṃ na ca vikṣipyate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the mind neither lapses into torpor nor is again distracted,

children.text: aniṅganam anābhāsaṃ niṣpannaṃ brahma tat tadā // MandUpK_3.46 //
children.translated_text: When it is motionless and without appearance — then it has become <s>Brahman</s>. // <s>MandUpK</s> 3.46 //

children.text: svasthaṃ śāntaṃ sanirvāṇam akathyaṃ sukham uttamam /
children.translated_text: Self-established, peaceful, with <s>nirvāṇa</s> (cessation), inexpressible, the supreme bliss,

children.text: ajam ajena jñeyena sarvajñaṃ paricakṣate // MandUpK_3.47 //
children.translated_text: Unborn, [known] through the unborn and knowable — they call it the omniscient. // <s>MandUpK</s> 3.47 //

children.text: na kaścij jāyate jīvaḥ saṃbhavo 'sya na vidyate /
children.translated_text: No <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) whatsoever is born; there is no origination of it.

children.text: etat tad uttamaṃ satyaṃ yatra kiñcin na jāyate // MandUpK_3.48 //
children.translated_text: This is that supreme truth where nothing whatsoever is born. // <s>MandUpK</s> 3.48 //

children.text: jñānenākāśakalpena dharmānyo gaganopamān /
children.translated_text: By knowledge that is like space, [knowing] <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that are like the sky,

children.text: jñeyābhinnena saṃbuddhas taṃ vande dvipadāṃ varam // MandUpK_4.1 //
children.translated_text: The fully awakened one, non-different from the knowable — I salute him, the best among bipeds. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.1 //

children.text: asparśayogo vai nāma sarvasattvasukho hitaḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Asparśayoga</s> (the yoga of non-contact) — such indeed is its name — beneficial and blissful for all beings;

children.text: avivādo 'viruddhaś ca deśitas taṃ namāmy aham // MandUpK_4.2 //
children.translated_text: Free from dispute and non-contradictory — thus it has been taught. I bow to it. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.2 //

children.text: bhūtasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ kecid eva hi /
children.translated_text: Certain disputants indeed wish for the birth of what already exists (<s>bhūta</s>),

children.text: abhūtasyāpare dhīrā vivadantaḥ parasparam // MandUpK_4.3 //
children.translated_text: While other wise ones, disputing with each other, [wish for the birth] of what does not exist (<s>abhūta</s>). // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.3 //

children.text: bhūtaṃ na jāyate kiñcid abhūtaṃ naiva jāyate /
children.translated_text: Nothing that exists is born; what does not exist is also never born.

children.text: vivadanto 'dvayā hy evam ajātiṃ khyāpayanti te // MandUpK_4.4 //
children.translated_text: The non-dualists, disputing thus, thereby proclaim non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>). // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.4 //

children.text: khyāpyamānām ajātiṃ tair anumodāmahe vayam /
children.translated_text: We approve of the non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) proclaimed by them;

children.text: vivadāmo na taiḥ sārdham avivādaṃ nibodhata // MandUpK_4.5 //
children.translated_text: We do not dispute with them — know this to be free from dispute. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.5 //

children.text: ajātasyaiva dharmasya jātim icchanti vādinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The disputants wish for the birth of what is by nature unborn (<s>ajāta</s>);

children.text: ajāto hy amṛto dharmo martyatāṃ katham eṣyati // MandUpK_4.6 //
children.translated_text: How will a <s>dharma</s> (reality) that is unborn and immortal come to mortality? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.6 //

children.text: na bhavaty amṛtaṃ martyaṃ na martyam amṛtaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The immortal does not become mortal, nor does the mortal become immortal;

children.text: prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathañcid bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.7 //
children.translated_text: A change in one's fundamental nature will never occur in any way. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.7 //

children.text: svabhāvenāmṛto yasya dharmo gacchati martyatām /
children.translated_text: How will that <s>dharma</s> which is by nature immortal come to be mortal?

children.text: kṛtakenāmṛtas tasya kathaṃ sthāsyati niścalaḥ // MandUpK_4.8 //
children.translated_text: When made [mortal] by artificial means, how will the immortal remain stable? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.8 //

children.text: sāṃsiddhikī svābhāvikī sahajā akṛtā ca yā /
children.translated_text: That which is accomplished, natural, innate, and uncreated —

children.text: prakṛtiḥ seti vijñeyā svabhāvaṃ na jahāti yā // MandUpK_4.9 //
children.translated_text: That should be known as <s>prakṛti</s> (essential nature) — which does not abandon its own nature. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.9 //

children.text: jarāmaraṇanirmuktāḥ sarve dharmāḥ svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are by nature free from old age and death;

children.text: jarāmaraṇam icchantaś cyavante tanmanīṣayā // MandUpK_4.10 //
children.translated_text: Those who wish for old age and death fall away through that very thinking. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.10 //

children.text: kāraṇaṃ yasya vai kāryaṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya jāyate /
children.translated_text: That for which the effect is the cause — the cause of that [itself] is born;

children.text: jāyamānaṃ katham ajaṃ bhinnaṃ nityaṃ kathaṃ ca tat // MandUpK_4.11 //
children.translated_text: If the cause is being born, how is it unborn? And if distinct [from the effect], how is it eternal? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.11 //

children.text: kāraṇād yady ananyatvam ataḥ kāryam ajaṃ yadi /
children.translated_text: If the effect is non-different from the cause — then the effect would be unborn;

children.text: jāyamānād dhi vai kāryāt kāraṇaṃ te kathaṃ dhruvam // MandUpK_4.12 //
children.translated_text: But if the effect is being born, how can your cause be permanent? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.12 //

children.text: ajād vai jāyate yasya dṛṣṭāntas tasya nāsti vai /
children.translated_text: For one who holds that something is born from the unborn — no illustration is possible;

children.text: jātāc ca jāyāmānasya na vyavasthā prasajyate // MandUpK_4.13 //
children.translated_text: And if something is born from what is [already] born, an infinite regress follows. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.13 //

children.text: hetor ādiḥ phalaṃ yeṣām ādir hetuḥ phalasya ca /
children.translated_text: For those for whom the fruit is the beginning of the cause, and the cause is the beginning of the fruit —

children.text: hetoḥ phalasya cānādiḥ kathaṃ tair upavarṇyate // MandUpK_4.14 //
children.translated_text: How can the beginninglessness of cause and fruit be described by them? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.14 //

children.text: hetor ādiḥ phalaṃ yeṣām ādir hetuḥ kalasya ca /
children.translated_text: For those for whom the fruit is the beginning of the cause, and the cause is the beginning of the fruit —

children.text: tathā janma bhavet teṣāṃ putrāj janma pitur yathā // MandUpK_4.15 //
children.translated_text: For them, birth would occur [in the same way] as the birth of a father from a son. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.15 //

children.text: saṃbhave hetuphalayor eṣitavyaḥ kramas tvayā /
children.translated_text: In the case of the origination of cause and effect, you must search for the sequence;

children.text: yugapatsaṃbhave yasmād asaṃbandho viṣāṇavat // MandUpK_4.16 //
children.translated_text: For in simultaneous origination, there is no connection — like [two] horns [of an animal, which do not cause each other]. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.16 //

children.text: phalād utpadyamānaḥ san na te hetuḥ prasidhyati /
children.translated_text: Your cause, being produced from the effect, is not established;

children.text: aprasiddhaḥ kathaṃ hetuḥ phalam utpādayiṣyati // MandUpK_4.17 //
children.translated_text: How will a cause that is not established produce an effect? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.17 //

children.text: yadi hetoḥ phalāt siddhiḥ phalasiddhiś ca hetutaḥ /
children.translated_text: If the cause is established through the effect, and the effect is established through the cause,

children.text: katarat pūrvaniṣpannaṃ yasya siddhir apekṣayā // MandUpK_4.18 //
children.translated_text: Which of the two was produced first, on which the establishment of the other depends? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.18 //

children.text: aśaktir aparijñānaṃ kramakopo 'tha vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Incapacity, lack of knowledge, or breach of sequence — or again,

children.text: evaṃ hi sarvathā buddhair ajātiḥ paridīpitā // MandUpK_4.19 //
children.translated_text: Thus in every way, non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) has been illuminated by the wise. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.19 //

children.text: bījāṅkurākhyo dṛṣṭāntaḥ sadā sādhyasamo hi sa /
children.translated_text: The illustration of the seed and sprout is always equal to what is to be proved (<s>sādhya</s>);

children.text: na hi sādhyasamo hetuḥ siddhau sādhyasya yujyate // MandUpK_4.20 //
children.translated_text: For a reason (<s>hetu</s>) that is equal to what is to be proved is not valid for establishing the <s>sādhya</s>. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.20 //

children.text: pūrvāparāparijñānam ajāteḥ paridīpakam /
children.translated_text: The non-apprehension of before and after illuminates non-origination;

children.text: jāyamānād dhi vai dharmāt kathaṃ pūrvaṃ na gṛhyate // MandUpK_4.21 //
children.translated_text: For how is the 'before' of a <s>dharma</s> that is being born not grasped? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.21 //

children.text: svato vā parato vāpi na kiñcid vastu jāyate /
children.translated_text: Nothing whatsoever is born — whether from itself or from another;

children.text: sad asat sadasad vāpi na kiñcid vastu jāyate // MandUpK_4.22 //
children.translated_text: Whether existent, non-existent, or both existent and non-existent — nothing whatsoever is born. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.22 //

children.text: hetur na jāyate 'nādeḥ phalaṃ cāpi svabhāvataḥ /
children.translated_text: A cause that is beginningless does not give rise [to anything], and the effect too [does not arise] from its own nature;

children.text: ādir na vidyate yasya tasya hy ādir na vidyate // MandUpK_4.23 //
children.translated_text: That which has no beginning — for that, indeed, no beginning is found. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.23 //

children.text: prajñapteḥ sanimittatvam anyathā dvayanāśataḥ /
children.translated_text: The having-a-cause of designation [is maintained] — otherwise, from the destruction of the pair [of subject and object],

children.text: saṃkleśasyopalabdheś ca paratantrāstitā matā // MandUpK_4.24 //
children.translated_text: The dependent existence [of phenomena] is held because of the apprehension of affliction (<s>saṃkleśa</s>). // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.24 //

children.text: prajñapteḥ sanimittatvam iṣyate yuktidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: The having-a-cause of designation is accepted from the standpoint of reasoning;

children.text: nimittasyānimittatvam iṣyate bhūtadarśanāt // MandUpK_4.25 //
children.translated_text: The causelessness of the cause is accepted from the standpoint of reality. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.25 //

children.text: cittaṃ na saṃspṛśaty arthaṃ nārthābhāsaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: The mind does not contact a [real] object, nor an appearance of an object;

children.text: abhūto hi yataś cārtho nārthābhāsas tataḥ pṛthak // MandUpK_4.26 //
children.translated_text: For the object is indeed unreal, and the appearance of an object is not separate from it. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.26 //

children.text: nimittaṃ na sadā cittaṃ saṃspṛśaty adhvasu triṣu /
children.translated_text: The mind never contacts a cause in the three times [past, present, future];

children.text: animitto viparyāsaḥ kathaṃ tasya bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.27 //
children.translated_text: How then can there be a delusion for it that is without cause? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.27 //

children.text: tasmān na jāyate cittaṃ cittadṛśyaṃ na jāyate /
children.translated_text: Therefore the mind is not born, and what is seen by the mind is not born;

children.text: tasya paśyanti ye jātiṃ khe vai paśyanti te padam // MandUpK_4.28 //
children.translated_text: Those who see the birth of that — they see a footprint in the sky. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.28 //

children.text: ajātaṃ jāyate yasmād ajātiḥ prakṛtis tataḥ /
children.translated_text: Since the unborn is [said to be] born, non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>) is its [true] nature;

children.text: prakṛter anyathābhāvo na kathañcid bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.29 //
children.translated_text: A change in one's fundamental nature will never occur in any way. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.29 //

children.text: anāder antavattvaṃ ca saṃsārasya na setsyati /
children.translated_text: The endedness of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), which is beginningless, will not be established;

children.text: anantatā cādimato mokṣasya na bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.30 //
children.translated_text: And the endlessness of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), which has a beginning, will not hold. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.30 //

children.text: ādāvante ca yan nāsti vartamāne 'pi tat tathā /
children.translated_text: That which does not exist at the beginning or at the end — likewise does not exist in the present.

children.text: vitathaiḥ sadṛśāḥ santo 'vitathā iva lakṣitāḥ // MandUpK_4.31 //
children.translated_text: Though resembling what is false, they are perceived as though real. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.31 //

children.text: saprayojanatā teṣāṃ svapne vipratipadyate /
children.translated_text: Their purposefulness is contradicted in a dream;

children.text: tasmād ādyantavattvena mithyaiva khalu te smṛtāḥ // MandUpK_4.32 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, by virtue of having a beginning and an end, they are indeed considered illusory. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.32 //

children.text: sarve dharmā mṛṣā svapne kāyasyāntanidarśanāt /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are false in a dream, since [one sees] within the confines of the body;

children.text: saṃvṛtte 'smin pradeśe vai bhūtānāṃ darśanaṃ kutaḥ // MandUpK_4.33 //
children.translated_text: In this enclosed space, how could there be perception of [real] beings? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.33 //

children.text: na yuktaṃ darśanaṃ gatvā kālasyāniyamād gatau /
children.translated_text: It is not reasonable that one perceives [something real] after going [there], because of the irregularity of time in going [there];

children.text: pratibuddhaś ca vai sarvas tasmin deśe na vidyate // MandUpK_4.34 //
children.translated_text: And certainly no one, upon awakening, exists in that [dream] place. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.34 //

children.text: mitrādyaiḥ saha saṃmantrya saṃbuddhau na prapadyate /
children.translated_text: What was deliberated with friends and others is not found upon waking;

children.text: gṛhītaṃ cāpi yat kiñcit pratibuddho na paśyati // MandUpK_4.35 //
children.translated_text: And whatever was grasped [in the dream] — the awakened one does not see it. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.35 //

children.text: svapne cāvastukaḥ kāyaḥ pṛthag anyasya darśanāt /
children.translated_text: In a dream, the body is insubstantial, because other [bodies] are seen separately;

children.text: yathā kāyas tathā sarvaṃ cittadṛśyam avastukam // MandUpK_4.36 //
children.translated_text: Just as the body [is insubstantial], so too everything perceived by the mind is insubstantial. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.36 //

children.text: grahaṇāj jāgaritavat taddhetuḥ svapna iṣyate /
children.translated_text: Because of apprehension [in both states], dream is considered to have the waking state as its cause;

children.text: tad dhetutvāt tu tasyaiva sajjāgaritam iṣyate // MandUpK_4.37 //
children.translated_text: But because it is the cause of that [dream], only for that [dreamer] is the waking state [considered] real. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.37 //

children.text: utpādasyāprasiddhatvād ajaṃ sarvam udāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: Because origination is not established, all is declared to be unborn;

children.text: na ca bhūtād abhūtasya saṃbhavo 'sti kathañcana // MandUpK_4.38 //
children.translated_text: And there is no origination whatsoever of the non-existent from the existent. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.38 //

children.text: asaj jāgarite dṛṣṭvā svapne paśyati tanmayaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having seen what is non-existent in the waking state, one absorbed therein sees it in dream;

children.text: asatsvapne 'pi dṛṣṭvā ca pratibuddhau na paśyati // MandUpK_4.39 //
children.translated_text: And having seen what is non-existent in dream as well, upon awakening one does not see it. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.39 //

children.text: nāsty asaddhetukam asat sadasaddhetukaṃ tathā /
children.translated_text: The non-existent does not have the non-existent as its cause; likewise, the existent does not have the non-existent as its cause;

children.text: sac ca saddhetukaṃ nāsti saddhetukam asat kutaḥ // MandUpK_4.40 //
children.translated_text: And the existent does not have the existent as its cause — how then can the non-existent have the existent as its cause? // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.40 //

children.text: viparyāsād yathā jāgrad acintyān bhūtavat spṛśet /
children.translated_text: Just as in the waking state, through delusion, one contacts inconceivable things as though real,

children.text: tathā svapne viparyāsād dharmāṃs tatraiva paśyati // MandUpK_4.41 //
children.translated_text: So too in dream, through delusion, one sees <s>dharmas</s> there alone. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.41 //

children.text: upalambhāt samācārād asti vastutvavādinām /
children.translated_text: Because of apprehension and conventional usage, those who assert the reality of things [teach thus];

children.text: jātis tu deśitā buddhair ajātes trasatāṃ sadā // MandUpK_4.42 //
children.translated_text: But birth has been taught by the <s>Buddhas</s> for those who are always frightened by non-origination (<s>ajāti</s>). // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.42 //

children.text: ajātes trasatāṃ teṣām upalambhād viyanti ye /
children.translated_text: For those who are frightened by non-origination, those who deviate because of [their attachment to] apprehension —

children.text: jātidoṣā na setsyanti doṣo 'py alpo bhaviṣyati // MandUpK_4.43 //
children.translated_text: The defects of [the doctrine of] birth will not befall them; moreover, the defect will be slight. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.43 //

children.text: upalambhāt samācārān māyāhastī yathocyate /
children.translated_text: Just as a magical elephant is said [to exist] because of apprehension and conventional usage,

children.text: upalambhāt samācārād asti vastu tathocyate // MandUpK_4.44 //
children.translated_text: So too a [real] thing is said [to exist] because of apprehension and conventional usage. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.44 //

children.text: jātyābhāsaṃ calābhāsaṃ vastvābhāsaṃ tathaiva ca /
children.translated_text: The appearance of birth, the appearance of movement, and the appearance of thingness —

children.text: ajācalam avastutvaṃ vijñānaṃ śāntam advayam // MandUpK_4.45 //
children.translated_text: Non-origination, immovability, non-thingness — <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is peaceful and non-dual. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.45 //

children.text: evaṃ na jāyate cittam evaṃ dharmā ajāḥ smṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus the mind is not born; thus <s>dharmas</s> are declared unborn;

children.text: evam eva vijānanto na patanti viparyaye // MandUpK_4.46 //
children.translated_text: Those who know thus do not fall into delusion. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.46 //

children.text: ṛjuvakrādikābhāsam alātaspanditaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a whirling firebrand appears as straight, curved, and other [shapes],

children.text: grahaṇagrāhakābhāsaṃ vijñānaspanditaṃ tathā // MandUpK_4.47 //
children.translated_text: So too the vibration of consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) appears as the grasped and the grasper. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.47 //

children.text: aspandamānam alātam anābhāsam ajaṃ yathā /
children.translated_text: Just as a firebrand that is not whirling is without appearance and unborn,

children.text: aspandamānaṃ vijñānam anābhāsam ajaṃ tathā // MandUpK_4.48 //
children.translated_text: So too consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>) that is not vibrating is without appearance and unborn. // <s>MandUpK</s> 4.48 //

children.text: alāte spandamāne vai nābhāsā anyato bhuvaḥ /
children.translated_text: When the firebrand (<s>alāta</s>) is in motion, the appearances (<s>ābhāsāḥ</s>) do not come from anywhere else;

children.text: na tato 'nyatra nispandān nālātaṃ praviśanti te // MandUpK_4.49 //
children.translated_text: nor do they go elsewhere when it is still, nor do they enter into the firebrand itself.

children.text: na nirgatā alātāt te dravyatvābhāvayogataḥ /
children.translated_text: They have not issued forth from the firebrand, because they lack substantiality (<s>dravyatva</s>);

children.text: vijñāne 'pi tathaiva syur ābhāsasyāviśeṣataḥ // MandUpK_4.50 //
children.translated_text: the same applies to <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) as well, since there is no difference in the nature of the appearances.

children.text: vijñāne spandamāne vai nābhāsā anyatobhuvaḥ /
children.translated_text: When <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness) is in motion, the appearances do not come from anywhere else;

children.text: na tato 'nyatra nispandān na vijñānaṃ viśanti te // MandUpK_4.51 //
children.translated_text: nor do they go elsewhere when it is still, nor do they enter into consciousness.

children.text: na nirgatās te vijñānād dravyatvābhāvayogataḥ /
children.translated_text: They have not issued forth from consciousness, because they lack substantiality;

children.text: kāryakāraṇatābhāvād yato 'cintyāḥ sadaiva te // MandUpK_4.52 //
children.translated_text: since causality (<s>kāryakāraṇatā</s>) is absent, they are forever inconceivable (<s>acintyāḥ</s>).

children.text: dravyaṃ dravyasya hetuḥ syād anyad anyasya caiva hi /
children.translated_text: A substance could be the cause of another substance, and one thing could be the cause of another;

children.text: dravyatvam anyabhāvo vā dharmāṇāṃ nopapadyate // MandUpK_4.53 //
children.translated_text: but substantiality or otherness of <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) is not logically tenable.

children.text: evaṃ na cittajā dharmāś cittaṃ vāpi na dharmajam /
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are not born from mind, nor is mind born from <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: evaṃ hetuphalājātiṃ praviśanti manīṣiṇaḥ // MandUpK_4.54 //
children.translated_text: thus the wise enter into the non-origination of cause and effect (<s>hetuphalājāti</s>).

children.text: yāvad dhetuphalāveśas tāvad dhetuphalodbhavaḥ /
children.translated_text: So long as there is attachment to cause and effect, there is the arising of cause and effect;

children.text: kṣīṇe hetuphalāveśe nāsti hetuphalodbhavaḥ // MandUpK_4.55 //
children.translated_text: when attachment to cause and effect is exhausted, there is no arising of cause and effect.

children.text: yāvad dhetuphalāveśaḥ saṃsāras tāvadāyataḥ /
children.translated_text: So long as there is attachment to cause and effect, <s>saṃsāra</s> extends onward;

children.text: kṣīṇe hetuphalāveśe saṃsāraṃ na prapadyate // MandUpK_4.56 //
children.translated_text: when attachment to cause and effect is exhausted, one does not enter into <s>saṃsāra</s>.

children.text: saṃvṛtyā jāyate sarvaṃ śāśvataṃ nāsti tena vai /
children.translated_text: By conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛti</s>), everything is born; therefore nothing is eternal;

children.text: sadbhāvena hy ajaṃ sarvam ucchedas tena nāsti vai // MandUpK_4.57 //
children.translated_text: in ultimate reality (<s>sadbhāvena</s>), everything is unborn (<s>aja</s>); therefore there is no annihilation.

children.text: dharmā ya iti jāyante jāyante te na tattvataḥ /
children.translated_text: The <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) that appear to be born are not born in reality (<s>tattvataḥ</s>);

children.text: janma māyopamaṃ teṣāṃ sā ca māyā na vidyate // MandUpK_4.58 //
children.translated_text: their birth is like <s>māyā</s> (illusion), and even that <s>māyā</s> does not exist.

children.text: yathā māyāmayād bījāj jāyate tanmayoṅkuraḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as from a seed that is itself conjured by <s>māyā</s>, a sprout of the same nature arises,

children.text: nāsau nityo na cocchedī tadvad dharmeṣu yojanā // MandUpK_4.59 //
children.translated_text: that sprout is neither eternal nor subject to annihilation — the same reasoning applies to all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena).

children.text: nājeṣu sarvadharmeṣu śāśvatāśāśvatābhidhā /
children.translated_text: With regard to all <s>dharmas</s> that are unborn (<s>aja</s>), the designations 'eternal' and 'non-eternal' do not apply;

children.text: yatra varṇā na vartante vivekas tatra nocyate // MandUpK_4.60 //
children.translated_text: where words (<s>varṇāḥ</s>) do not function, no distinction (<s>viveka</s>) can be predicated.

children.text: yathā svapne dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ calati māyayā /
children.translated_text: Just as in dream, the mind moves through <s>māyā</s> with the appearance of duality (<s>dvayābhāsa</s>),

children.text: tathā jāgrad dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ calati māyayā // MandUpK_4.61 //
children.translated_text: so too in waking, the mind moves through <s>māyā</s> with the appearance of duality.

children.text: advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ cittaṃ svapne na saṃśayaḥ /
children.translated_text: In dream, the mind is non-dual (<s>advaya</s>) yet appears as duality — there is no doubt;

children.text: advayaṃ ca dvayābhāsaṃ tathā jāgran na saṃśayaḥ // MandUpK_4.62 //
children.translated_text: in waking too, the mind is non-dual yet appears as duality — there is no doubt.

children.text: svapnadṛk pracaran svapne dikṣu vai daśasu sthitān /
children.translated_text: The dreamer, moving about in the dream, sees beings situated in all ten directions —

children.text: aṇḍajān svedajān vāpi jīvān paśyati yān sadā // MandUpK_4.63 //
children.translated_text: egg-born, sweat-born, and other living beings (<s>jīvāḥ</s>) — always.

children.text: svapnadṛkcittadṛśyās te na vidyante tataḥ pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Those are perceived by the dreamer's mind and do not exist apart from it;

children.text: tathā tad dṛśyam evedaṃ svapnadṛkcittam iṣyate // MandUpK_4.64 //
children.translated_text: likewise, all that is perceived is accepted as being nothing but the dreamer's mind.

children.text: carañ jāgarite jāgrad dikṣu vai daśasu sthitān /
children.translated_text: The waking person, moving about in the waking state, sees beings situated in all ten directions —

children.text: aṇḍajān svedajān vāpi jīvān paśyati yān sadā // MandUpK_4.65 //
children.translated_text: egg-born, sweat-born, and other living beings — always.

children.text: jāgrac cittekṣaṇīyās te na vidyante tataḥ pṛthak /
children.translated_text: Those are perceived by the waking mind and do not exist apart from it;

children.text: tathā tad dṛśyam evedaṃ jāgrataś cittam iṣyate // MandUpK_4.66 //
children.translated_text: likewise, all that is perceived is accepted as being nothing but the waking mind.

children.text: ubhe hy anyonyadṛśye te kiṃ tad astīti cocyate /
children.translated_text: Both states are mutually perceived by each other — what then can be said to truly exist?

children.text: lakṣaṇāśūnyam ubhayaṃ tan mate naiva gṛhyate // MandUpK_4.67 //
children.translated_text: Both are devoid of defining characteristics (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>); neither can be grasped according to this view.

children.text: yathā svapnamayo jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Just as a dream-born being (<s>jīva</s>) is born and also dies,

children.text: tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca // MandUpK_4.68 //
children.translated_text: so all these beings come into existence and cease to exist.

children.text: yathā māyāmayo jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Just as a being conjured by <s>māyā</s> (illusion) is born and also dies,

children.text: tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca // MandUpK_4.69 //
children.translated_text: so all these beings come into existence and cease to exist.

children.text: yathā nirmitako jīvo jāyate mriyate 'pi ca /
children.translated_text: Just as a magically created (<s>nirmitaka</s>) being is born and also dies,

children.text: tathā jīvā amī sarve bhavanti na bhavanti ca // MandUpK_4.70 //
children.translated_text: so all these beings come into existence and cease to exist.

children.text: na kaścij jāyate jīvaḥ saṃbhavo 'sya na vidyate /
children.translated_text: No <s>jīva</s> (individual self) whatsoever is born; there is no origination for it.

children.text: etat tad uttamaṃ satyaṃ yatra kiñcin na jāyate // MandUpK_4.71 //
children.translated_text: This is that supreme truth — where nothing whatsoever is born.

children.text: cittaspandikam evedaṃ grāhyagrāhakavad dvayam /
children.translated_text: This duality of grasped and grasper (<s>grāhyagrāhaka</s>) is merely the vibration of mind (<s>cittaspandita</s>);

children.text: cittaṃ nirviṣayaṃ nityam asaṅgaṃ tena kīrtitam // MandUpK_4.72 //
children.translated_text: the mind is without object (<s>nirviṣaya</s>), eternal; therefore it is declared to be unattached (<s>asaṅga</s>).

children.text: yo 'sti kalpitasaṃvṛtyā paramārthena nāsty asau /
children.translated_text: That which exists by imagined convention (<s>kalpitasaṃvṛti</s>) does not exist in ultimate reality (<s>paramārtha</s>);

children.text: paratantrābhisaṃvṛtyā syān nāsti paramārthataḥ // MandUpK_4.73 //
children.translated_text: that which exists by dependent convention (<s>paratantrābhisaṃvṛti</s>) does not exist in ultimate reality.

children.text: ajaḥ kalpitasaṃvṛtyā paramārthena nāpy ajaḥ /
children.translated_text: The unborn (<s>aja</s>) exists only by imagined convention; in ultimate reality, it is not even 'unborn';

children.text: paratantrādiniṣpattyā saṃvṛtyā jāyate tu saḥ // MandUpK_4.74 //
children.translated_text: by virtue of arising through dependent origination and other processes, it is born only conventionally (<s>saṃvṛtyā</s>).

children.text: abhūtābhiniveśo 'sti dvayaṃ tatra na vidyate /
children.translated_text: There is fixation on the unreal (<s>abhūtābhiniveśa</s>), but duality does not exist therein;

children.text: dvayābhāvaṃ sa buddhvaiva nirnimitto na jāyate // MandUpK_4.75 //
children.translated_text: having realized the absence of duality, one is without cause (<s>nirnimitta</s>) and is not born.

children.text: yadā na labhate hetūn uttamādhamamadhyamān /
children.translated_text: When the mind does not find causes — superior, inferior, or middling —

children.text: tadā na jāyate cittaṃ hetvabhāve phalaṃ kutaḥ // MandUpK_4.76 //
children.translated_text: then the mind is not born; in the absence of cause, whence could an effect arise?

children.text: animittasya cittasya yānutpattiḥ samādvayā /
children.translated_text: That non-arising (<s>anutpatti</s>) of the causeless mind, which is the same and non-dual (<s>samā advayā</s>) —

children.text: ajātasyaiva sarvasya cittadṛśyaṃ hi tadyataḥ // MandUpK_4.77 //
children.translated_text: that is because everything is unborn (<s>ajāta</s>), and what is perceived is nothing but mind.

children.text: buddhvā nimittatāṃ satyāṃ hetuṃ pṛthag anāpnuvan /
children.translated_text: Having realized the true nature of causation, yet not apprehending any separate cause,

children.text: vītaśokaṃ tathākāmam abhayaṃ padam aśnute // MandUpK_4.78 //
children.translated_text: one attains the state that is free from sorrow (<s>vītaśoka</s>), free from desire (<s>akāma</s>), and free from fear (<s>abhaya</s>).

children.text: abhūtābhiniveśād dhi sadṛśe tat pravartate /
children.translated_text: Due to fixation on the unreal (<s>abhūtābhiniveśa</s>), the mind engages with what appears real;

children.text: vastvabhāvaṃ sa budhvaiva niḥsaṅgaṃ vinivartate // MandUpK_4.79 //
children.translated_text: having realized the non-existence of objects (<s>vastvabhāva</s>), it turns back, free from attachment (<s>niḥsaṅga</s>).

children.text: nivṛttasyāpravṛttasya niścalā hi tathā sthitiḥ /
children.translated_text: When it has ceased and does not engage again, its state is truly unwavering (<s>niścalā</s>);

children.text: viṣayaḥ sa hi buddhānāṃ tat sāmyam ajam advayam // MandUpK_4.80 //
children.translated_text: that is the domain of the awakened ones (<s>buddhāḥ</s>) — that is the unborn (<s>aja</s>), non-dual (<s>advaya</s>) sameness (<s>sāmya</s>).

children.text: ajam anidram asvapnaṃ prabhātaṃ bhavati svayam /
children.translated_text: Unborn (<s>aja</s>), without sleep (<s>anidra</s>), without dream (<s>asvapna</s>), it is self-luminous (<s>prabhāta</s>) by itself;

children.text: sakṛdvibhāto hy evaiṣa dharma dhātusvabhāvataḥ // MandUpK_4.81 //
children.translated_text: for this <s>dharma</s> (reality) is forever radiant by the very nature of the <s>dhātu</s> (fundamental element).

children.text: sukham āvriyate nityaṃ duḥkhaṃ vivriyate sadā /
children.translated_text: Happiness is always concealed and suffering is always revealed,

children.text: yasya kasya ca dharmasya graheṇa bhagavān asau // MandUpK_4.82 //
children.translated_text: for the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord) is obscured by the grasping of any <s>dharma</s> whatsoever.

children.text: asti nāsty asti nāstīti nāsti nāstīti vā punaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'It exists,' 'it does not exist,' 'it exists and does not exist,' or again 'it does not exist at all' —

children.text: calasthirobhayābhāvair āvṛṇotye va bāliśaḥ // MandUpK_4.83 //
children.translated_text: through the notions of moving, still, both, or neither — the ignorant one (<s>bāliśa</s>) covers it over.

children.text: koṭhyaś catasra etās tu grahair yāsāṃ sadā vṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: These are the four positions (<s>koṭhyaḥ</s>) by whose grasp one is always enveloped;

children.text: bhagavān ābhir aspṛṣṭo yena dṛṣṭaḥ sa sarvadṛk // MandUpK_4.84 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Lord) is untouched by these — one who sees this is the all-seer (<s>sarvadṛk</s>).

children.text: prāpya sarvajñatāṃ kṛtsnāṃ brāhmaṇyaṃ padam advayam /
children.translated_text: Having attained complete omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>), the non-dual state of <s>Brahman</s> (<s>brāhmaṇya pada</s>),

children.text: anāpannādimadhyāntaṃ kim ataḥ param īhate // MandUpK_4.85 //
children.translated_text: that which has no beginning, middle, or end — what more could one desire beyond this?

children.text: viprāṇāṃ vinayo hy eṣa śamaḥ prākṛta ucyate /
children.translated_text: This is the discipline (<s>vinaya</s>) of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (knowers of <s>Brahman</s>); this is called natural tranquility (<s>śama</s>);

children.text: damaḥ prakṛtidāntatvād evaṃ vidvāñ śamaṃ vrajet // MandUpK_4.86 //
children.translated_text: self-control (<s>dama</s>) comes from being naturally subdued — thus knowing, the wise one should abide in <s>śama</s> (peace).

children.text: savastu sopalambhaṃ ca dvayaṃ laukikam iṣyate /
children.translated_text: That which has objects (<s>savastu</s>) and involves apprehension (<s>sopalambha</s>) — this duality is considered worldly (<s>laukika</s>);

children.text: avastu sopalambhaṃ ca śuddhaṃ laukikam iṣyate // MandUpK_4.87 //
children.translated_text: that which is without objects yet still involves apprehension is considered the purified worldly (<s>śuddha laukika</s>).

children.text: avastv anupalambhaṃ ca lokottaram iti smṛtam /
children.translated_text: That which is without objects and without apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) is regarded as supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>);

children.text: jñānaṃ jñeyaṃ ca vijñeyaṃ sadā buddhaiḥ prakīrtitam // MandUpK_4.88 //
children.translated_text: knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), the knowable (<s>jñeya</s>), and the to-be-known (<s>vijñeya</s>) — these are always proclaimed by the awakened ones (<s>buddhāḥ</s>).

children.text: jñāne ca trividhe jñeye krameṇa vidite svayam /
children.translated_text: When the threefold knowledge and the knowable are progressively realized by oneself,

children.text: sarvajñatā hi sarvatra bhavatīha mahādhiyaḥ // MandUpK_4.89 //
children.translated_text: omniscience (<s>sarvajñatā</s>) arises everywhere for the one of great intelligence (<s>mahādhī</s>).

children.text: heyajñeyāpyapākyāni vijñeyāny agrayāṇataḥ /
children.translated_text: That which is to be abandoned (<s>heya</s>), that which is to be known (<s>jñeya</s>), that which is to be attained (<s>āpya</s>), and that which is to be brought to maturity (<s>pākya</s>) — these are to be understood through the foremost vehicle (<s>agrayāna</s>);

children.text: teṣām anyatra vijñeyād upalambhas triṣu smṛtaḥ // MandUpK_4.90 //
children.translated_text: except for the 'to be known' (<s>vijñeya</s>), apprehension (<s>upalambha</s>) is attributed to the other three.

children.text: prakṛtyākāśavaj jñeyāḥ sarve dharmā anādayaḥ /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) are beginningless and are to be known as like space (<s>ākāśa</s>) by nature;

children.text: vidyate na hi nānātvaṃ teṣāṃ kvacana kiñcanaḥ // MandUpK_4.91 //
children.translated_text: there is no multiplicity (<s>nānātva</s>) whatsoever among them anywhere.

children.text: ādibuddhāḥ prakṛtyaiva sarve dharmāḥ suniścitāḥ /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> are primordially awakened (<s>ādibuddha</s>) by their very nature — this is firmly established;

children.text: yasyaivaṃ bhavati kṣāntiḥ so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate // MandUpK_4.92 //
children.translated_text: one who has such acceptance (<s>kṣānti</s>) is fit for immortality (<s>amṛtatva</s>).

children.text: ādiśāntā hy anutpannāḥ prakṛtyaiva sunirvṛtāḥ /
children.translated_text: Primordially peaceful (<s>ādiśānta</s>), unborn (<s>anutpanna</s>), by their very nature completely quiescent (<s>sunirvṛta</s>) —

children.text: sarve dharmāḥ samābhinnā ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradam // MandUpK_4.93 //
children.translated_text: all <s>dharmas</s> are equal (<s>sama</s>) and undifferentiated (<s>abhinna</s>); this is the unborn sameness (<s>aja sāmya</s>), the state of clarity (<s>viśārada</s>).

children.text: vaiśāradyaṃ tu vai nāsti bhede vicaratāṃ sadā /
children.translated_text: Clarity (<s>vaiśāradya</s>) indeed does not exist for those who always dwell in differentiation (<s>bheda</s>);

children.text: bhedanimnāḥ pṛthagvādās tasmāt te kṛpaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ // MandUpK_4.94 //
children.translated_text: those who are inclined toward differences and advocate separateness — they are declared to be pitiable (<s>kṛpaṇāḥ</s>).

children.text: aje sāmye tu ye kecid bhaviṣyanti suniścitāḥ /
children.translated_text: But those who will become firmly established in the unborn sameness (<s>aje sāmye</s>),

children.text: te hi loke mahājñānās tac ca loko na gāhate // MandUpK_4.95 //
children.translated_text: they are the ones of great knowledge (<s>mahājñāna</s>) in this world, and the world cannot fathom them.

children.text: ajeṣv ajam asaṃkrāntaṃ dharmeṣu jñānam iṣyate /
children.translated_text: Among the unborn <s>dharmas</s>, knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is accepted as unborn and non-transitioning (<s>asaṃkrānta</s>);

children.text: yato na kramate jñānam asaṅgaṃ tena kīrtitam // MandUpK_4.96 //
children.translated_text: since knowledge does not pass over to anything, it is declared to be unattached (<s>asaṅga</s>).

children.text: aṇumātre 'pi vaidharmye jāyamāne 'vipaścitaḥ /
children.translated_text: If even the slightest difference (<s>vaidharmya</s>) arises for the unwise (<s>avipaścit</s>),

children.text: asaṅgatā sadā nāsti kimutāvaraṇacyutiḥ // MandUpK_4.97 //
children.translated_text: non-attachment (<s>asaṅgatā</s>) is forever lost — how much less the falling away of obscurations (<s>āvaraṇacyuti</s>)?

children.text: alabdhāvaraṇāḥ sarve dharmāḥ prakṛtinirmalāḥ /
children.translated_text: All <s>dharmas</s> have never acquired obscurations (<s>āvaraṇa</s>) and are pure (<s>nirmala</s>) by nature;

children.text: ādau buddhās tathā muktā budhyanta iti nāyakāḥ // MandUpK_4.98 //
children.translated_text: they are primordially awakened (<s>ādibuddha</s>) and likewise liberated (<s>mukta</s>) — so declare the leaders (<s>nāyakāḥ</s>).

children.text: kramate na hi buddhasya jñānaṃ dharmeṣu tāyinaḥ /
children.translated_text: The knowledge of the <s>Buddha</s>, the protector (<s>tāyin</s>), does not pass over to <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena);

children.text: sarve dharmās tathā jñānaṃ naitad buddhena bhāṣitam // MandUpK_4.99 //
children.translated_text: all <s>dharmas</s> are likewise knowledge — this was not taught by the <s>Buddha</s> in this way.

children.text: durdarśam atigambhīram ajaṃ sāmyaṃ viśāradam /
children.translated_text: Hard to see (<s>durdarśa</s>), exceedingly profound (<s>atigambhīra</s>), unborn (<s>aja</s>), the sameness (<s>sāmya</s>), the state of clarity (<s>viśārada</s>) —

children.text: buddhvā padam anānātvaṃ namaskurmo yathābalam // MandUpK_4.100 //
children.translated_text: having realized this state of non-multiplicity (<s>anānātva</s>), we offer our salutations to the best of our ability.
